title: Where does the window start?
hook: Move a maximum window; keep track of which cells it includes.

doesNotKnow: With offset 1 and stride 2, what is the last pooled value?

misconception: The primary and materially changed case must have the same consequence.
objective: Compute the pooling stride construction and explain its countercase and stated boundary.

claims.text: Where does the window start? Move a maximum window; keep track of which cells it includes. With offset 1 and stride 2, what is the last pooled value? Options: 3; 8; 9.

claims.text: The shifted last window contained 3 and 8, producing 8. Both swapped pairs produced 9, although its original position changed. The maximum retained the value, not its within-window location. These valid-window examples do not establish translation invariance.

claims.text:
Target / packet: `ai-pooling-stride` · `B2`. Prerequisites: `ai:convolution-weight-sharing`.

Nearest / distinct payoff: `convolution-weight-sharing` → `convolution-weight-sharing` (earlier admitted draft or same-packet identity; not independent clearance). Unlike shared filter multiplication, this applies a maximum and loses within-window location under stride/offset changes.

Primary finite model: 1D activation[1,9,2,3,8], max window2. Offset0 stride2 gives[9,3]; offset1 gives[9,8]; stride1 offset0 gives[9,9,3,8].

Countercase and boundary: Inputs[9,1] and[1,9] both pool to9: within-window location lost. No claim that pooling is strictly translation invariant.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict output count and last maximum after offset change; recall which of the two positions can be recovered from a pooled value of 9 alone.

Required evidence: Show window membership and retain lost-location counterexample; labels distinguish offset from stride. Shipped local computations, all cases: Pool: window=2 · offset=0 · stride=2 1 9 2 3 8 [1,9]→9 [2,3]→3; o0 s2: [1,9] [2,3]→[9,3] | Shift: window=2 · offset=1 · stride=2 1 9 2 3 8 [9,2]→9 [3,8]→8; o1 s2: [9,2] [3,8]→[9,8] | Stride1: window=2 · offset=0 · stride=1 1 9 2 3 8 [1,9]→9 [9,2]→9 [2,3]→3 [3,8]→8; o0 s1: [1,9] [9,2] [2,3] [3,8]→[9,9,3,8] | Swap: window=2 · offset=0 · stride=2 9 1 [9,1]→9 [1,9]→9 = [9,1]→9; [9,1]→9; [1,9]→9. Initial neutral frame: window=2 · offset=0 · stride=2 1 9 2 3 8.
